Note that if $\mathcal{K}_F$ is an isometry, but not unitary, then the spectrum of $\mathcal{K}_F$ is the unit disc and $\spec_{\mathrm{ap}}(\mathcal{K}_F)=\mathbb{T}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|=1\}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound is stated for an arbitrary epsilon-pseudoeigenfunction (unit g with ||(K_F-lambda)g||<=epsilon) with no restriction on lambda or ||K_F||. Telescoping gives ||K_F^n g - lambda^n g|| <= epsilon * sum_{j=0}^{n-1} |lambda|^{n-1-j} ||K_F||^j, which is Theta(n epsilon) only when |lambda|<=1 and ||K_F||<=1. Counterexample inside the paper's own setting: for a measure-preserving non-invertible system such as the doubling map, K_F is an isometry with Sp_ap = T (unit circle); taking lambda = 1+epsilon/2 gives sigma_inf(K_F - lambda) = dist(lambda, T) = epsilon/2, so a unit g with ||(K_F-lambda)g|| <= epsilon exists, yet ||K_F^n g - lambda^n g|| >= |lambda|^n - 1 = (1+epsilon/2)^n - 1, growing exponentially in n rather than O(n epsilon).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses ||K_F|| <= 1 and |lambda| <= 1; then the telescoping estimate gives the exact bound n epsilon. These hypotheses hold for the measure-preserving applications the formula motivates.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed physical-relevance guarantee for pseudoeigenfunctions is false as written (even for measure-preserving systems, whenever |lambda|>1, and for dissipative systems with ||K_F||>1). It is used only as motivation; no theorem depends on it.
issues.title: Pseudoeigenfunction evolution bound O(n epsilon) is false without |lambda|<=1 and contractivity
issues.why_classification: Adding standard local hypotheses makes the claim correct with no change to any result; the display plays no inferential role elsewhere.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inclusions do not follow from the last-visit rule. If the sequence h_{n_2,j}(z,F) visits I^1 once and then remains in the open gap (epsilon-1/n_2, epsilon+1/(2n_2)) converging to, say, epsilon+1/(4n_2), the last visit is in I^1, so z is included in Gamma_{n_2}(F), yet h_{n_2}(z,F) > epsilon, violating the second inclusion. If the sequence visits I^2 early and then converges to a value in (epsilon-1/n_2, epsilon-1/(2n_2)), the last visit is in I^2, so z is excluded although h_{n_2}(z,F) < epsilon-1/(2n_2), violating the first inclusion. The inclusions that actually hold are {h_{n_2} < epsilon-1/n_2} subset Gamma_{n_2} subset {h_{n_2} <= epsilon+1/(2n_2)}, which only give Gamma_{n_2} subset Sp_{ap,epsilon+1/(2n_2)}; since Sp_{ap,epsilon+delta} does not approach Sp_{ap,epsilon} at any uniform rate over the general class Omega_X, the stated conclusion that the tower is Sigma_2^G (containment in Sp_{ap,epsilon} up to computable error 2^{-n_2}) is not established by the written construction.

\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\!\Gamma_n(F)\!=\!\begin{dcases}
1,\!\!&\text{if $\exists$ a non-trivial eigenfunction},\\
0,\!\!&\text{otherwise},

An eigenfunction $g\in\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$ is non-trivial. A system is weakly mixing precisely when there are no non-trivial eigenfunctions.

issues.failure_explanation: Part (a) is false for every skew product F(x,y) = (x, y+f(x)): any nonconstant function of x alone is invariant, e.g., g(x,y) = sin(x) satisfies K_F g = g, lies in span{1}^perp, and its spectral measure is a point mass at 1 (hence not continuous). So every such F has non-trivial eigenfunctions (eigenvalue 1 with infinite multiplicity) and Xi_p^dec(F) = 1 on the entire adversarial family; such systems are never ergodic, let alone weakly mixing. What is true (visible from the Fourier expansion in y: g_k(x) e^{ikf(x)} = lambda g_k(x) forces g_k = 0 for k != 0 when f is strictly increasing) is that 1 is the ONLY eigenvalue, which is what salvages Sp_pp(K_{F_f}) = {1} for the Xi_p lower bound and lemma (b) is correct. But the proof of the second classification of thm:torus requires stages with Xi_p^dec(F_{f^{(k)}}) = 0, which this family can never provide, so the alternation argument for {Xi_p^dec, Omega_p}^{Delta_1} not in Delta_2^P collapses.

failure_location.quote: If $f$ is strictly increasing on $[-\pi,0]$, the spectral measure of $\mathcal{K}_F$ with respect to any $g\in L^2(\mathcal{X},\omega)$ is continuous on $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$. It follows that there are no eigenfunctions in the subspace $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must (i) weaken technical_lemma3(a) to the true statement (1 is the only eigenvalue, with eigenfunctions the functions of x, and spectral measures continuous only off the invariant subspace), and (ii) prove the Xi_p^dec lower bound via a new adversarial family inside Omega_p that alternates between weakly mixing maps and maps with non-trivial eigenvalues while agreeing on finite data. Skew products over a fixed or periodically driven coordinate cannot supply the weakly mixing side (they always admit non-trivial eigenfunctions), so the repair requires something on the order of Anosov-Katok weakly mixing diffeomorphisms C^infinity-close to rotations, a construction not present in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound for the decision problem of detecting non-trivial eigenfunctions (thm:torus's second classification, and thm4's first impossibility claim) loses its proof, together with the headline prose that rests on it (the abstract's 'non-trivial eigenfunctions ... cannot be determined by any sequence of (even randomized) algorithms', the thm4 summary bullet, the third row of fig:proof_ideas, the corresponding region of fig:SCI2, and the Discussion's 'detecting non-trivial eigenfunctions'). The Sigma_2 upper bounds for both problems and the lower bound for the pure point spectrum Xi_p are independent of the false statement and survive, so only 'SCI <= 2' remains established for the decision problem.
issues.title: technical_lemma3(a) is false: skew products (x,y)->(x,y+f(x)) always have non-trivial eigenfunctions, breaking the eigenfunction-detection lower bound
issues.why_classification: The false lemma statement is the load-bearing premise for the impossibility half of one of the paper's flagship results (advertised in the abstract and thm4). No local edit restores the claimed alternation, and the source contains no alternative construction; the claim must either be abandoned (loss of an advertised central result) or reproved with essentially new proof architecture.
